metadata.title: The MOND Acceleration Scale from MeerKAT: 47 Deep-Regime HI Discs in MIGHTEE-HI COSMOS
metadata.description:
Version 1.0 (draft for review; not peer reviewed).

The programme ties the MOND acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, not derived; its footings are canonical a0 = 9.3603e-11 (rho_Lambda) and alternative 1.1312e-10 m s^-2 (rho_crit). We run a framework-native width chain, frozen before any width was read, on the public MeerKAT MIGHTEE-HI COSMOS catalogue (293 HI sources): W50 and inclination give V, the baryons are 1.33 M_HI + M* at half the HI diameter, and a median-residual estimator with the nu_mono kernel returns a0.

Result. 47 golden discs survive, all deep in the MOND regime (g_bar/a0 <= 0.084) and 37 gas-dominated; four calibration controls pass, among them a SPARC closure of the baryon side (+0.008 dex). The pooled scale is a0 = 1.046e-10 m s^-2 (bootstrap 68% 1.01-1.15; recipe half-width +-0.143 dex): +0.048 dex from the canonical footing, -0.034 dex from the alternative and -0.060 dex from SPARC's 1.20; kappa = 0.56 (rho_Lambda) or 0.46 (rho_crit). The direct V^4/(G M_b) is 1.25e-10 (1.19 for the gas-dominated discs), which includes the kernel's next-order factor (+0.078 dex).

The dominant systematic: the HI flux scale. The released cubes confirm the catalogue widths (-0.022 dex, scatter 0.039 dex) but hold less flux. Arecibo single-dish (ALFALFA) fluxes for 15 overlapping galaxies exceed the catalogue's by 0.195 dex (the catalogue holds 0.64 of them) and the cubes' by more, so the cube scale is not supported; if that offset carried over to our fainter, more distant sample, a0 would fall to about 0.6-0.75e-10. On present evidence the flux scale places a0 between about 0.6 and 1.05e-10, the catalogue value at the top; the velocity frame of the catalogue widths could add +0.098 dex.

What it can and cannot say. On the catalogue's flux scale the result is consistent with SPARC and with both footings; on the single-dish scale it would lie below both. It does not separate the footings and, at z <= 0.093, cannot test the constant a0(z) the framework predicts (the rival's lever is 0.009 dex). The cold mass (Omega_c h^2 ~ 0.12) is still required; no dark-matter particle is added; nothing here says the data favour the framework.

Every number carried by an audit row is re-read from committed files by PAPER40_audit.py (306 of 306; ten literature values are checked only for being printed); the post hoc rows come from make_paper40_figures.py, which first reproduces the lane's committed values exactly. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed.
